clue.text: Hard liquor out of order in driest parts (13, two words)

indicators.note: things out of order are jumbled, so the following words must be rearranged

blocks.note: all thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Strong drink is banned in the driest regions of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent spirits is an old phrase for distilled alcoholic drinks such as whisky or gin, which is what hard liquor means.

clue.text: Something like a poncho, in Peru an 'anorak'

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: the letters run across Peru and an

explanation.surface: In Peru a garment much like a poncho is what passes for an anorak.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruana is a woollen, cape-like overgarment worn in South America, very similar to a poncho.

clue.text: Clippings of dishevelled and grubby sheep, what shearer removes?

definitions.text: Clippings of dishevelled and grubby sheep, what shearer removes

indicators.note: clipping each word down to its first piece leaves just its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A shearer trims away the filthy matted bits from a scruffy sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the first letters of four words, and a description of what a shearer cuts off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dags are the dung-clotted locks of wool round a sheep's rear, which are clipped off when shearing.

clue.text: It was used to disguise obscenity applied to noun in US city

definitions.text: It was used to disguise obscenity

indicators.note: the preceding pieces are placed inside the place name that follows

blocks.note: on, as in placed on top of

explanation.surface: A rude word was disguised by the euphemism used in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonny is the meaningless refrain word (as in hey nonny no) that old songs used to veil bawdy meanings.

clue.text: Those who've tied the knot, unnatural in poetic language

blocks.note: first meaning: the wed, married people, read as two words
second meaning: a Spenserian word for mannered or affected

explanation.walkthrough: Split as THE WED it names married couples; as one word it is an old poetic term meaning mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used thewed to mean having particular manners, i.e. mannered, and mannered behaviour is affected or unnatural.

clue.text: Versatile cookery ingredient, what lumberjack suggests to audience

indicators.note: what reaches an audience is heard, so we go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: a lumberjack might say 'saw you', in casual speech 'saw ya'

explanation.surface: A flexible kitchen staple is recommended by a woodsman to his listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya beans give flour, milk, sauce and tofu, making the bean an all-purpose ingredient in cooking.

clue.text: First in perspicacity? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the first letter in the following word is the one wanted

blocks.note: rats! is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that certain people lead in shrewdness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue mocks the idea that fools are the sharpest minds; prat is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prats are idiots, so calling them first in perspicacity is an ironic jibe at people with no insight.

clue.text: Vicar getting Helen up – it signals break of day

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the name from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A clergyman wakes Helen with a dawn alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning, so it announces daybreak.

clue.text: One entering ripped a hanging garland

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so this letter is placed within the next word

explanation.surface: Someone coming in tore down a festoon of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a torana is a festoon or garland strung across a gateway, so it is literally a hanging decoration.

clue.text: Type of laver to observe round a minced cutlet (10, two words)

indicators.note: mincing chops something up, so the letters of the next word are scrambled
the verb goes round the rest, with its letters either side

explanation.surface: A seaweed recipe tells you to watch over some chopped meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lettuce is a green seaweed of the genus Ulva, which goes by the name green laver.

clue.text: Possible treatment for snakebite from Antigua cobra

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out from within the words that follow, across their join

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A remedy for a venomous bite comes from a Caribbean snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Guaco is a tropical American climbing plant whose leaves were used as an antidote to snake venom.

clue.text: One showing astonishment about girl on piano, producer of polished finish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the onlooker word wraps round what follows

explanation.surface: An amazed spectator watches a girl seated at a piano with a gleaming lacquer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just puts the girl before the piano letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasspaper is abrasive sanding paper used to smooth wood to a polished finish.

clue.text: It's dragged round field (lucky thing with abandonment of spades) (8, two words)

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A charm is carried round a field once the gardening tools are given up.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that goes is the one after HORSE, the plural ending's spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse hoe is a hoe drawn by a horse between crop rows, so it is pulled across a field.

clue.text: Lake? Dip a rod in its fringes

indicators.note: dipping something puts it into something else, here into the outside letters
fringes are edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: its refers back to this word, whose edge letters are used
rod is American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: At a lake, someone lowers a fishing rod in at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake' does double duty: it is the definition, and 'its fringes' are its own first and last letters. 'Rod' is not a fishing rod but gangster slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagune is an old spelling of lagoon, a stretch of salt water cut off from the sea, effectively a lake.

clue.text: ARA dismissed by old king? That's disgusting

indicators.note: the letters that are dismissed are sent away from the word that follows

explanation.surface: An old monarch sacks the Royal Navy reserve, to general revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ARA out of the middle of PHARAOH.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoh is an interjection expressing disgust or contempt, so it is what one says for 'that's disgusting'.

clue.text: TV recorder in truth requiring outlay of capital?

indicators.note: an outlay is spent and gone, so that part leaves the word

explanation.surface: Telling the truth about a TV recorder might cost a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: VERA (Vision Electronic Recording Apparatus) was an early BBC videotape recorder.
explanation.definitionFit: VERA was an experimental BBC machine of the 1950s that recorded television pictures onto tape.

clue.text: Obnoxious fellow protecting a scheme for red-light district

indicators.note: protecting means enclosing, so the fellow wraps round what follows

blocks.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: A nasty man shields a racket for the city's sleazy quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapland is the Japanese term for an area of bathhouse brothels, i.e. a red-light district.

clue.text: Olympian? First-class, followed by another such?

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete is top class, and then comes another top performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian here means one of the gods of Mount Olympus, not a Games competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena, goddess of wisdom, was one of the twelve Olympian deities living on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Dog some day needs training

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A puppy will have to be trained one of these days.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian spitz breed, originally kept for herding and sledding.

clue.text: 'Love' inscribed in ring, mostly with simple elegance

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
an inscription is written within, so the letter goes inside the ring word

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A ring bears the engraved word 'Love' in an understated, graceful style.
explanation.definitionFit: Soigné means well-groomed and elegantly simple in dress or style.

clue.text: Exercising veto I'm showing purpose

indicators.note: exercising works something about, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Using my right to block something shows what I am after.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason or aim behind an action, a close synonym of purpose.

clue.text: Sort of insect, female going for husband like a rotter!

indicators.note: one thing going for another means it replaces it in the word

blocks.note: an insect whose larvae build cases

explanation.surface: A woman leaving her husband for a bug is treated as a heartless cad.
explanation.walkthrough: The F of the insect is replaced by H.
explanation.definitionFit: Caddishly means in the manner of a cad, a man who behaves dishonourably, which is what a rotter is.

clue.text: Decay? Counteracting treatment's anti this

explanation.surface: A remedy is said to oppose rot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'antidote is anti + this': what follows ANTI in the remedy's name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dote is a Chambers word for decay, especially rot in timber, and as a verb means to decay.

clue.text: Fierce bird's youth, accordingly accompanied by temper

explanation.surface: A young hawk is described as hot-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: In falconry, sorage is the first year of a hawk's life, before its first moult.

clue.text: Repeating Brit ack-ack gun

blocks.note: Australian slang for a British person
the same slang word said a second time

explanation.surface: A British soldier keeps firing an anti-aircraft weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeating' tells you to write the word for a Brit twice; Pom is Australian slang for a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: The pom-pom was a quick-firing automatic cannon, used in the Second World War as an anti-aircraft (ack-ack) gun.

clue.text: Dried fruit, some in pie including dash of booze

indicators.note: printer's pie is a jumble of loose type, so these letters are mixed up
a dash is a small amount, here just the first letter of the drink
including means taking inside, so the letter goes within the mixed letters

explanation.surface: A pie contains some dried fruit and a splash of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type.
explanation.definitionFit: Mebos is a South African sweetmeat of salted or sugared dried apricots.

clue.text: One from among notables worsted – such as Brutus?

indicators.note: taking one from among means removing the single letter meaning one
worsted means beaten, so the remaining letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: One of the dignitaries is defeated, like Brutus among Caesar's assassins.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony calls Brutus 'the noblest Roman of them all' in Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Antony names Brutus the most honourable of the conspirators, so Brutus is the type of the noblest.

clue.text: British composer failing to finish piece no longer current

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An English composer leaves a work unfinished, now out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is a coin, and 'current' means in currency, not modern.
explanation.definitionFit: The belga was a Belgian currency unit used between the World Wars, so it is a coin no longer in circulation.

clue.text: Number in grip of drink move with tottering gait

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it

explanation.surface: Someone in the grip of drink lurches along unsteadily.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing is to sway from side to side, which is what one does walking with an unsteady, rolling gait.

clue.text: Central American closed left eye

blocks.note: a door pushed to is shut
a private eye is a detective, slang tec

explanation.surface: A Mexican Indian has his left eye shut.
explanation.definitionFit: The Toltecs were a pre-Aztec people of central Mexico, so a Toltec is a Central American.

clue.text: Lively Scottish slang

blocks.note: first meaning: a Scots word for brisk or merry
second meaning: jargon of a particular group

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of lively Scots speech, but splits into a dialect adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, cant means lively or brisk; separately, cant is the private jargon or argot of a group.

clue.text: Deploying weather eye could make one this (tee-hee!)

definitions.text: Deploying weather eye could make one this (tee-hee!)

indicators.note: deploying means spreading out and arranging, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the bracketed laugh is the part of the jumble left over

explanation.surface: Keeping a weather eye open could make you cautious, with a little laugh at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of 'weather eye' rearrange to the answer plus 'tee-hee', and the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a weather eye open means staying watchful, so it makes a person cautious and on guard.

clue.text: Craving what's bad for you, not entirely atypical

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the next word is used

blocks.note: a run of letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Wanting unhealthy things is not completely unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a medical condition involving a craving to eat non-food substances such as earth or chalk.

clue.text: Typical of Greek poet, one of the people, college ingested

indicators.note: something ingested is swallowed, so it ends up inside the preceding word

explanation.surface: A typical Greek poet is a man of the people who has swallowed a college education.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcaic refers to the verse forms of Alcaeus, the Greek lyric poet of Lesbos.

clue.text: I cut cooked meat in e.g. service

indicators.note: cut means removed, so this letter is taken away from the meat
the shortened meat goes inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: deer meat as it comes to the table

explanation.surface: I carve the roast meat, for instance, at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Church of England, also called evening prayer.

clue.text: Minimum from relative in what you inherit, making you sneer?

indicators.note: the least part one can take from the word is its single opening letter
the letter is put inside the following hereditary unit

blocks.note: a unit of heredity that shapes a person

explanation.surface: An inherited trait from a family member makes you curl your lip.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerne is a Spenserian word meaning to grin or snarl, so close to a sneer.

clue.text: Pistol could have done for this yesterday, a dog running wild (13, three words)

definitions.text: Pistol could have done for this

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dog dashing about was startled by a gun fired yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pistol' is the starter's gun, not a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting pistol can replace the spoken race-start call, so the phrase is what a gun could have done for.
